editorNote: A money-and-infrastructure day: Anthropic's numbers get a fresh look, a SaaS vendor discloses a breach, and a grid mystery turns out to be batteries all checking the clock at once.

stories.headline: Anthropic's amended S-1 shows $17B in Q3 revenue, growth slowing, and $895B in compute commitments
stories.summary: CNBC reports Anthropic's updated filing puts Q3 revenue near $17B and nine-month revenue at $33.24B, with a $104B nine-month net loss mostly from fair-value changes on convertible notes and derivatives.
stories.whyItMatters: Quarterly growth was about 47% in Q3, down from 144% in Q2 and 132% in Q1, against roughly $895.4B in purchase and lease commitments, substantially all for compute.

sourceLinks.title: CNBC: Anthropic reports $17B in Q3 revenue in revised S-1

stories.headline: Trigger.dev says an attacker accessed customer environment variables
stories.summary: In a post dated November 1, Trigger.dev says an attacker used an exploit, now blocked, to gain unauthorized access to environment variables for a subset of organizations.
stories.whyItMatters: The post does not say how many organizations or which variables were affected; owners of affected accounts were emailed mitigation steps.

stories.headline: Mystery of the 60-second power-grid frequency dips traced to battery storage systems
stories.summary: Jülich-led researchers report in Nature Energy that large batteries checking their state of charge at the start of every minute create consumption spikes behind the regular one-minute dips.
stories.whyItMatters: The spikes can add wear to hydro turbines, and in Ireland the one-minute signal's amplitude quadrupled between 2016 and 2021; the proposed fix is to randomize the checks.

sourceLinks.title: Forschungszentrum Jülich: Mystery of 60-second fluctuations in power grids solved

stories.headline: Nibnib, an experimental image format, decodes two RGB565 pixels per byte for tiny microcontrollers
stories.summary: Raph Levien's repository describes a 4-bits-per-pixel format where each byte indexes a 256-entry palette of deltas, built for DVI output on an RP2350 with about 6 cycles per pixel.
stories.whyItMatters: The README gives no benchmark numbers, and the author calls it a basic, working technique not meant for archiving.
